eyebrow: Statistics & Probability for Data Science · Chapter 4, Lesson 18
subtitle: "39.6 minutes" hides how uncertain it is. A range tells the truth.

eyebrow: The recipe: estimate +/- critical value x SE
code:
sample = rng.choice(pop, size=40, replace=False)
xbar, se = sample.mean(), stats.sem(sample)   # 39.62, 0.863

tcrit = stats.t.ppf(0.975, df=39)   # 2.023
caption: 0.975 comes from splitting the remaining 5% into two 2.5% tails.

code:
print(xbar - tcrit*se, xbar + tcrit*se)   # 37.87  41.37
print(stats.t.interval(0.95, 39, loc=xbar, scale=se))   # same thing
caption: The true mean, 40.01, sits right inside this 95% interval.

eyebrow: The most misunderstood idea in statistics

steps.label: NOT: 95% chance truth is in THIS interval
steps.sub: The true mean is fixed -- in or out

steps.label: IT MEANS: the PROCEDURE succeeds 95% of the time

code:
hits = 0
for _ in range(2000):
    smp = rng.choice(pop, size=40, replace=False)
    l, h = stats.t.interval(0.95, 39, loc=smp.mean(), scale=stats.sem(smp))
    hits += (l <= pop.mean() <= h)
print(hits / 2000)   # 0.9475
caption: 2,000 separate intervals -- 94.75% of them actually caught the true mean.

code:
# conf   width
# 0.90   2.91
# 0.95   3.49
# 0.99   4.68  -- ~1/3 more width than 95% for just 4 more points of confidence
caption: Nothing is free: more confidence means a wider, less precise interval.
Each 4x increase in n roughly halves the width -- the same square-root rule as always.

code:
p = 120 / 400
se_p = np.sqrt(p * (1-p) / 400)
z = stats.norm.ppf(0.975)
print(p - z*se_p, p + z*se_p)   # 0.2551  0.3449
caption: Works poorly when n is small or p is near 0/1 -- check the Wilson interval for those cases.

eyebrow: When the recipe wobbles: skew + small n
code:
# very skewed log-normal pop, samples of only 15:
for _ in range(2000):
    smp = rng.choice(pop2, size=15, replace=False)
    l, h = stats.t.interval(0.95, 14, loc=smp.mean(), scale=stats.sem(smp))
    hits += (l <= pop2.mean() <= h)
# only 0.8575 -- the "95%" interval caught the mean just 86% of the time
caption: Fix: a larger sample, or the bootstrap (next lesson). A biased sample stays wrong regardless.

subtitle: A CI only covers random error -- a biased sample gives a confidently wrong interval.
